name: medium-core-off-power-loss-secondary
title: MLAG secondary power loss · Medium lab, STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
action: Resets the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH: protocol-mode=none and forward-reserved-addresses=no on both MLAG peers, protocol-mode=rstp priority=0x0000 on the access switch, with edge=yes on its uplink bond and edge=yes, bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on on its host port ether4, and reads the access switch port settings back. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, no BPDU from or through the MLAG pair and one copy of each broadcast. It then emulates a power loss of CHR 2 (MLAG secondary): in one step it takes the container veths behind CHR 2's ether2 to ether4 down, sets the facing NICs of CHR 1 and the access switch link-down over QMP and pauses CHR 2's guest with QMP stop, then confirms carrier loss at every neighbour. After 20 s it powers CHR 2 on with QMP system_reset and cont, brings the links back up, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: Secondary off
phases.expected: Every link to CHR 2 loses carrier at once, as on a real power loss. CHR 1 (MLAG primary) sees its peer port ether2 go down and keeps the shared system ID, so the access switch's uplink bond and traffic host 2 keep their LACP partner. They drop their member to CHR 2 on carrier loss, without waiting for the LACP short timeout. The uplink bond keeps one running member, so the access switch's edge bridge port keeps forwarding.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: Carrier returns while CHR 2 boots. CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the 802.3ad bond until the MLAG system ID syncs with CHR 1 (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The access switch re-adds the member to its forwarding edge uplink, so loss is brief or none.
